page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-8 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The memory configuration consists of 30.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 3.75 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_tile and AMX_int8), alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-core capabilities. It achieves top-tier status in Geekbench single-core performance with a score of 2256.0 and text processing at 2977.0. Single-threaded gzip compression at 35.04 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 15.25 GB/sec also place in the top 25% tier.

Multi-core and memory-bound workloads generally align with mid-range expectations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 8882.75 and Geekbench multi-core score of 8502.0 fall within the average category. Memory bandwidth tests show 690.5 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 61.57 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. For specialized tasks, the server performs exceptionally well in text generation using a small 135M LLM model at 352.64 tokens/sec, though performance drops to a weaker 7.21 tokens/sec when running a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4n-standard-8 offers a balanced resource profile for general-purpose compute workloads that benefit from dedicated Intel Xeon cores and advanced vector or matrix instructions without the overhead of local storage. The lack of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it a streamlined option for stateless applications. It is highly suitable for single-threaded processing tasks, text processing, web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference using small models.

Built on 4 physical cores with hyper-threading, it includes advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations. This instance does not bundle local storage or GPUs. Factual benchmark data highlights top-tier single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2256.0 and strong single-threaded compression speeds. While multi-core metrics and memory bandwidth align with mid-range averages, the server excels at small-model LLM text generation and text processing. It represents a resource-dense, cost-efficient option for stateless workloads, web serving, and single-threaded applications requiring dedicated CPU execution.
